title: Scenario pack frontmatter
description: Validates the optional YAML frontmatter of a Specify acceptance scenario file. Discovery roots and opt-in semantics are defined in `acceptance/README.md` §Scenario Discovery; the discoverer in `scripts/checks.ts` only validates files that live under one of those roots and start with frontmatter. Bodies of opted-in scenarios follow the §Scenario Pack Shape sections (`Intent`, `Workspace`, `Inputs`, `Invocation`, `Expected Artifacts`, `Assertions`, `Negative Expectations`, `Cleanup`).

id.description: Globally unique scenario identifier (kebab-case). Cross-file uniqueness is enforced in `scripts/checks.ts`.

owner.description: The capability, plugin, skill, or suite that owns this scenario (kebab-case).

kind.description: Open enum. C03 actively validates `capability` and `capability-boundary`; `suite` and `skill` are accepted so C06/skill-fixture promotions can opt in without re-touching this schema.

capability.description: Versioned capability identifier, e.g. `contracts@v1`. Required when `kind` is `capability` or `capability-boundary` (enforced by allOf below).

backend.description: Which runner backend executes this scenario. `manual` documents a human-driven scenario; `fixture` materialises a known expected-artifact set for runner-only smoke tests (C05); `stub` (C08) drives slice phase outcomes through `specify` CLI calls; `scripted-plan` (C09) drives `specify change plan {create, add}` from a fixture brief to produce a deterministic stand-in for `/change:plan` that the role-based plan assertions can score; `scripted-execute` (C10) layers a deterministic `/change:execute loop` equivalent on top of `scripted-plan` so the execute-* assertions exercise end-to-end; `scripted-finalize` (C11) layers `workspace push` + fake-`gh` mark-merged + `change finalize` + idempotency probe on top of `scripted-execute` so the push-* / finalize-* assertions exercise end-to-end; `contracts-build` (C13) layers per-slice phase-driver dispatch on top of `scripted-execute` so the contract slice emits a deterministic-but-realistic OpenAPI 3.1 + JSON Schema bundle the contracts WASI tool can validate, while implementation slices stay on the stub driver; `omnia-build` (C14a) extends the per-slice dispatch so Omnia-capability slices emit a deterministic Rust crate skeleton (`Cargo.toml` + `src/lib.rs` + `src/providers.rs`) into the routed clone's `crates/<crate>/` tree while the contract slice still runs through `ContractsBuildPhaseDriver` and other slices stay on the stub; `vectis-build` (C14b) extends the per-slice dispatch so Vectis-capability slices emit a deterministic Vectis composition + SwiftUI shell (`composition.yaml` at the project root + `apps/mobile/<screen>.swift` residue file) into the routed clone while the contract slice still runs through `ContractsBuildPhaseDriver` and other slices stay on the stub; `agent` and `recorded` gate later runner backends. Passing `--backend X` for a scenario whose frontmatter declares a different backend is a hard error unless `--allow-backend-mismatch` is set.

stages.description: Slice phases the scenario exercises. Must be a contiguous prefix of `[define, build, merge, drop]` starting at `define`; the prefix rule is enforced in `scripts/checks.ts` because JSON Schema cannot express ordering without combinatorial enums.

isolation.description: Workspace isolation contract for the scenario.

assertions.description: Optional list of named assertion ids the runner dispatches. Free-form kebab-case strings.

expected-artifacts.description: Optional list of relative artifact paths produced by the scenario. Path-safety (relative, no `..`, no absolute) is enforced in `scripts/checks.ts`.

negative-expectations.description: Forbidden-condition ids. Required (with at least one entry) when `kind` is `capability-boundary`.

stubbed-stages.description: Subset of `stages` that the deterministic stub backend (C08) drives via the `specify` CLI. Each entry maps to a deterministic CLI sequence (`slice transition`, optional fixture materialisation, `slice merge run`). Only valid when `backend: stub`. Cross-field invariants — must be a subset of `stages` and only appears with `backend: stub` — are enforced in `scripts/checks.ts` because JSON Schema cannot express inter-field rules cleanly.

stub-fixtures.description: Optional per-stage fixture directory (repo-relative) the stub backend copies into the workspace at the start of a stubbed stage. Keys are stage names (`define` / `build` / `merge`); values are paths under the repo root (e.g. `acceptance/fixtures/<scenario-id>/expected`). Required when a build/merge stage is stubbed AND `expected-artifacts` is non-empty; the stub backend fails with `runner-setup` otherwise.
